title: ERC-8262 provider evidence
description: Served at GET https://{trustDomainId}/v1/erc8262/evidence/{evidenceId} (SPEC.md section 10.4). Unsigned: fetching from the allowlisted trust domain's host over https, without redirects, is the authentication, and a callback or push only announces an evidenceId. Acceptance authorizes nothing until the on-chain proof it feeds has verified and its public inputs match this document (SPEC.md section 10.5, proof_mismatch). Carries identifiers and bindings only: no PII, documents, applicant ids or provider payloads. Every field except status and revokedAt is immutable per (trustDomainId, evidenceId). Body at most 8192 bytes.

protocolVersion.description: Provider protocol version; equals the `/v{n}/erc8262/` path segment. A consumer MUST refuse a version it does not implement.

evidenceId.description: Replay: an unguessable capability (at least 128 bits, base64url), unique for the provider's lifetime and never reused. A consumer validates an announced id against this rule before using it, requests exactly `https://{trustDomainId}/v1/erc8262/evidence/` followed by the id, and refuses a body whose evidenceId differs (exact comparison). It keys what it has observed by (trustDomainId, evidenceId). Re-delivery with identical immutable fields is idempotent and counts once; any differing immutable field is refused. Renewal is a new evidenceId.

status.description: Revocation: `active` or `revoked`, monotonic. Once a consumer observes `revoked` (or a 410 for the id) it MUST NOT accept the evidenceId again, whatever a later response says. Expiry is computed from expiresAt, never signalled here.

revokedAt.description: Unix seconds; present iff status is `revoked`.

subject.description: Replay: the wallet (lowercase hex) the claim is about and the only submitter it may serve; ERC-8262 credentials and signed payloads bind the submitter.

sourceId.description: The commercial evidence source (the vendor whose check produced the claim), e.g. `sumsub`. The same sourceId may appear under several trust domains (a vendor reached natively and through a gateway); quorum never counts sourceIds.

claimType.description: The claim, namespaced `<namespace>.<name>`, e.g. `kyc.individual`, `personhood.unique`. Consumers map (sourceId, claimType) to their own scoring policy; a provider never sends points, categories or tiers.

policyId.description: The provider's verification policy under which the claim was established (e.g. a KYC level). Immutable per id: a change in what the provider checks is a new policyId, never an edit. Distinct from the consumer's scoring policy version, which a provider never sends.

trustDomainId.description: The independently controlled signing domain: the lowercase DNS host that serves this provider's discovery document and evidence endpoint. A document is authoritative only when fetched over https, without redirects, from this exact host: the consumer compares the serialized host of the URL it fetched with this value as exact ASCII. Never an IP literal: the last label starts with a letter, so no WHATWG URL parser reads the host as an IPv4 address. The host proves nothing about the attestor: the consumer's allowlist pins each trust domain to its attestorProviderId per Oracle deployment, and a host it does not list is refused.

deployment.description: An ERC-8262 Oracle deployment and this trust domain's attestor on it. chainId and oracleAddress bind every artifact to one deployment (ERC-8262 signed payloads and credential roots are deployment-scoped), so evidence for one chain or Oracle is never accepted on another.

attestorProviderId.description: The ERC-8262 Oracle `providerId` (uint256: nonzero and at most 2^256 - 1) that attests for this trust domain on the paired deployment, as a canonical decimal string. Self-asserted: a consumer accepts it only when it equals the attestor its allowlist pins for the trust domain.

keyId.description: Rotation: the discovery key that produced the artifact, matched exactly (case-sensitive) against discovery keyIds. issuedAt MUST fall inside that key's [notBefore, notAfter) window, the key MUST NOT be revoked (by keyId or key material), and a signed-signals key (proof types 7-9) MUST NOT be retired at evaluation time.

issuedAt.description: Unix seconds. May lead the consumer's clock by at most 60 seconds.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds, exclusive; greater than issuedAt and at most 31536000 seconds (365 days) after it.

artifact.description: What the claim feeds on-chain. Type 4 names its credential root; types 7-9 are signed per proof by the key named in keyId. The proof a consumer relies on MUST match it: the same proofType and submitter == subject; type 4 provider_id == deployment.attestorProviderId, credential_type == credentialType and credential_root == credentialRoot; types 7/8 signer_pubkey_hash, and for type 9 one of the active signer slots, == the keyId key's signerPubkeyHash. Its timestamp lies in [issuedAt - 60 s, expiresAt), and its Oracle attestation is unrevoked and unexpired.

credentialRoot.description: The published root containing the subject's credential leaf. Valid only while the Oracle reports it registered to attestorProviderId, not revoked (revokeCredentialRoot is on-chain revocation) and inside its 48-hour CREDENTIAL_ROOT_TTL.
